subject: science
title: How water moves through a plant

cards.front: Where does a plant take in water?
cards.back: Through its roots, from the soil.
cards.say: Where does a plant take in water? Through its roots, from the soil.

cards.front: Which part carries water up the plant?
cards.back: The stem.
cards.say: Which part carries water up the plant? The stem.

cards.front: Where does water go after it travels up the stem?
cards.back: To the leaves and other parts of the plant.
cards.say: Where does water go after it travels up the stem? To the leaves and other parts of the plant.

cards.front: Which way does water travel in a stem?
cards.back: Upwards, from the roots to the leaves.
cards.say: Which way does water travel in a stem? Upwards, from the roots to the leaves.

cards.front: Why do plants need water?
cards.back: Water keeps the plant firm and helps it make food and grow.
cards.say: Why do plants need water? Water keeps the plant firm and helps it make food and grow.

cards.front: What happens to a plant that does not get enough water?
cards.back: It wilts. The leaves and stem droop and go soft.
cards.say: What happens to a plant that does not get enough water? It wilts. The leaves and stem droop and go soft.

cards.front: wilt
cards.back: To droop and go soft because there is not enough water.
cards.say: wilt. To droop and go soft because there is not enough water.

cards.front: How can you show that water moves up a stem?
cards.back: Stand a white flower in water with coloured dye. After some hours the petals show the colour.
cards.say: How can you show that water moves up a stem? Stand a white flower in water with coloured dye. After some hours the petals show the colour.

cards.front: In the coloured water test, why do the petals change colour?
cards.back: The coloured water travelled up the stem to the petals.
cards.say: In the coloured water test, why do the petals change colour? The coloured water travelled up the stem to the petals.

cards.front: Do roots take in water from the air or the soil?
cards.back: From the soil. Roots take in water from the ground around them.
cards.say: Do roots take in water from the air or the soil? From the soil. Roots take in water from the ground around them.

cards.front: Why do cut flowers last longer in a vase of water?
cards.back: The stems keep taking up water, so the flowers do not wilt so quickly.
cards.say: Why do cut flowers last longer in a vase of water? The stems keep taking up water, so the flowers do not wilt so quickly.

cards.front: What should you do to help a wilted pot plant?
cards.back: Give it water. The roots take it in and the plant becomes firm again.
cards.say: What should you do to help a wilted pot plant? Give it water. The roots take it in and the plant becomes firm again.

cards.front: Do all parts of a plant need water?
cards.back: Yes. Roots, stem, leaves and flowers all need water.
cards.say: Do all parts of a plant need water? Yes. Roots, stem, leaves and flowers all need water.

cards.front: Why might a plant in a dry place have long roots?
cards.back: Long roots can reach water deep under the ground.
cards.say: Why might a plant in a dry place have long roots? Long roots can reach water deep under the ground.

cards.front: True or false: A plant takes in most of its water through its leaves.
cards.back: False. A plant takes in most water through its roots.
cards.say: True or false: A plant takes in most of its water through its leaves. False. A plant takes in most water through its roots.

cards.front: What is the order water follows in a plant?
cards.back: Roots, then stem, then leaves.
cards.say: What is the order water follows in a plant? Roots, then stem, then leaves.

cards.front: Why is celery good for showing water movement?
cards.back: Its pale stalk shows the coloured water clearly as it moves up.
cards.say: Why is celery good for showing water movement? Its pale stalk shows the coloured water clearly as it moves up.

cards.front: How does a stem help the leaves?
cards.back: It carries water up to them and holds them up in the light.
cards.say: How does a stem help the leaves? It carries water up to them and holds them up in the light.

cards.front: What is a good way to keep a pot plant healthy?
cards.back: Water it regularly and put it where it gets light.
cards.say: What is a good way to keep a pot plant healthy? Water it regularly and put it where it gets light.

cards.front: What happens to the leaves if the roots cannot take in water?
cards.back: The leaves droop and may dry out.
cards.say: What happens to the leaves if the roots cannot take in water? The leaves droop and may dry out.

cards.front: Why do roots have many thin parts called root hairs?
cards.back: Root hairs help the root take in more water from the soil.
cards.say: Why do roots have many thin parts called root hairs? Root hairs help the root take in more water from the soil.

cards.front: Does water move up a stem very fast or slowly?
cards.back: Fairly slowly. In the coloured water test you wait some hours to see the colour.
cards.say: Does water move up a stem very fast or slowly? Fairly slowly. In the coloured water test you wait some hours to see the colour.

cards.front: Which part of the plant is under the soil taking in water?
cards.back: The roots.
cards.say: Which part of the plant is under the soil taking in water? The roots.

cards.front: What do we call the movement of water from the roots up to the leaves?
cards.back: Water moving up the stem. It happens all the time in a healthy plant.
cards.say: What do we call the movement of water from the roots up to the leaves? Water moving up the stem. It happens all the time in a healthy plant.
